results.prompt: Make a mono green storm deck in Premodern.
results.text:
I built and submitted a mono-green storm deck for Premodern. It's an untested brew, not a proven list, and no tournament results exist for it.

**The plan.** Premodern has only two green storm cards, Hunting Pack and Sprouting Vines. Hunting Pack costs 7 and makes a 4/4 Beast, plus one more for each spell cast before it this turn. The deck floods mana with free or untap spells, which also build the storm count. Then it casts Hunting Pack, with Concordant Crossroads giving the Beasts haste. Concordant Crossroads reads "All creatures have haste." Overrun (+3/+3 and trample) finishes through blockers.

**Key cards**
- **Mana engine.** Rofellos taps for G per Forest. Emerald Charm (untap target permanent), Vitalize (untap all your creatures), Seeker of Skybreak and Quirion Ranger can all untap Rofellos or elves for another tap. Early Harvest untaps all your basic lands, so it adds mana and storm count.
- **Cheap storm fuel.** Lotus Petal and Land Grant (free if you hold no lands) cost little or nothing. Insist costs G and draws a card, and Worldly Tutor can find Rofellos.
- **Finishers.** There are four Hunting Pack, two Concordant Crossroads and two Overrun. Hunting Pack is an instant, so you can also cast it at the end of an opponent's turn and attack with the Beasts on your own turn. That works without Crossroads.
- **Card flow.** Two Sylvan Library.

**Mana.** The deck runs 16 Forests, 8 one-mana elves and 3 Lotus Petals. check_deck's land-count suggestion of about 19.7 is a generic formula that doesn't account for the elves, Petals and untap spells. I stayed at 16, all Forests, because Rofellos and Early Harvest want them.

**Odds.** With 4 Hunting Pack, you see at least one by turn 5 on the play about 57% of the time. You see at least one of Rofellos or the two Seekers about 46% of the time. Both together is about 25%. It is a fast but fragile deck with no protection from counterspells or hand disruption.

**Sideboard (15)**
- **Enchantress (the top deck in the results, 12.5%):** 2 Tranquility and 2 Naturalize. Both hit my own Sylvan Library and Crossroads too, so side out those cards.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** 2 Moment's Peace and 2 Fog, to survive a turn or two.
- **Stiflenought (artifact-based):** 2 Crumble and 1 Seeds of Innocence.
- **Faster mana:** 2 Mox Diamond, plus 1 Seedborn Muse and 1 Gaea's Blessing as extras.

If you face a slow control deck, bring in the Mox Diamonds and keep the Fogs in the sideboard.

**Unverified.** I did not test the deck against the meta lists. Card legality and text come from the card tools. The Premodern results had no data on Hunting Pack decks, so I can't say how the deck performs in practice.

**Plan:** Play Goblins on turn 1 with Goblin Lackey and Mogg Fanatic, then use Goblin Warchief and Goblin Piledriver to hit hard. Goblin Matron and Goblin Ringleader refill your hand. Rishadan Port and Wasteland slow the opponent's mana. Gempalm Incinerator, Mogg Fanatic and Goblin Sharpshooter clear small blockers. Siege-Gang Commander and Goblin Tinkerer are the late-game power.

**Key cards:** All of these are in nearly every list in the archetype data.
- **Goblin Lackey, Goblin Piledriver, Goblin Warchief, Mogg Fanatic:** four copies each, in 100% of lists.
- **Gempalm Incinerator and Siege-Gang Commander:** also in 100% of lists. This list runs four Incinerators and three Commanders.
- **Goblin Matron:** four copies, in about 97% of lists. It tutors for Warchief, Sharpshooter or Tinkerer as needed.
- **Goblin Ringleader:** four copies, in about 99% of lists.
- **Rishadan Port and Wasteland:** in about 99% and 97% of lists.
- **One-ofs:** Goblin Sharpshooter, Goblin Tinkerer and Skirk Prospector are the singleton tools. Skirk Prospector adds mana, and Goblin Tinkerer can destroy an artifact.

**Mana:** 24 lands in total. That is 17 Mountain, 4 Rishadan Port and 3 Wasteland, which is 17.5 red sources by the tool's count. The archetype averages about 24 lands and about 17 red sources. The 47% of lists that splash green for Naturalize use Karplusan Forest and Wooded Foothills. This list stays mono-red and keeps its answers in the sideboard.

**Sideboard (15):**
- **3 Tormod's Crypt:** against Replenish and graveyard decks like Hermit Druid Combo.
- **3 Pyrokinesis:** against small creatures. This is the card for Sligh, and the other aggro decks that Goblins' bigger bodies can race.
- **3 Red Elemental Blast and 2 Overload:** against Stiflenought and UB Psychatog, which are blue decks. These cards are for the blue matchups, and I haven't checked their exact text here. Overload is aimed at artifacts such as Stifle's Nought.
- **2 Anarchy:** against Enchantress and the white-based decks.
- **1 Goblin Goon:** extra beef after sideboarding.
- **1 Mogg Salvage:** against artifact-heavy decks.

The meta data shows Enchantress at 12.5%, Terrageddon at 11.2%, Stiflenought at 10.4% and Sligh at 9.9% over the last 30 days. Goblins itself is at 4.4%.

I did not check rules text for individual cards beyond the legality and mana check, so the sideboard roles above rest on the archetype's usual choices.

results.prompt: Build a Replenish deck in Premodern that doesn't play blue.
results.text:
I built a mono-white Replenish deck with no blue. It's a brew, so it has no tournament record. `check_deck` passed with no errors or warnings. Its only comparison note was about land count and blue sources, which don't apply to this build.

**Plan.** The usual Replenish deck fills its graveyard with blue cards: Attunement, Intuition, Frantic Search and Decree of Silence. This list uses Lion's Eye Diamond instead. Hold Opalescence, Parallax Wave and other enchantments in hand. Cast Replenish with four mana. With Replenish on the stack, activate Lion's Eye Diamond to discard your whole hand, then Replenish returns every enchantment you discarded. Opalescence turns them into creatures, and Parallax Wave exiles blockers. The returned enchantments are summoning-sick, so the win comes a turn later.

**Key cards.**
- **Lion's Eye Diamond** (4) is the discard outlet. **Mox Diamond** (3) and **Ancient Tomb** (4, adds {C}{C}) get Replenish out early. **Serra's Sanctum** (2) adds {W} for each enchantment you control.
- **Enlightened Tutor** (4) fetches the missing artifact or enchantment, usually Opalescence or Lion's Eye Diamond. It puts the card on top of your library, so it costs you a draw.
- **Opalescence** (4) and **Parallax Wave** (4) are the core. The big enchantments are Angelic Chorus, Worship, Righteous Cause and Mobilization. Under Opalescence they become creatures with power and toughness equal to their mana value, and Worship keeps you alive at 1 life while you control one.
- **Swords to Plowshares** (4) and **Seal of Cleansing** (3) cover the early game and artifact decks like Stiflenought. **Abeyance** (2) cantrips. **Rune of Protection: Red** (2) helps against Sligh and Goblins, and you can cycle it for {2} when you don't need it.

**Mana.** 19 lands: 13 Plains, 4 Ancient Tomb and 2 Serra's Sanctum. That's 22 sources once you add Mox Diamond and Lion's Eye Diamond. The deck has no blue card selection, so it plays fewer lands than the 25 average in tournament Replenish lists. The tool recommended about 21.5 lands, and I stayed at 19 because the Moxes and Lion's Eye Diamond ramp. Expect more mulligans and awkward hands than the blue version.

**Sideboard (15).** The meta data shows Enchantress, Terrageddon, Stiflenought, Sligh and Hermit Druid as the top decks.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** Circle of Protection: Red (2), Story Circle (1), Wrath of God (2) and Exalted Angel (2).
- **Stiflenought and Terrageddon:** Abolish (2) and Disenchant (1) for artifacts and enchantments. Orim's Chant (2) stops a key spell or an attack.
- **Hermit Druid and Psychatog:** Tormod's Crypt (2).
- **Humility (1):** a one-of, held for creature decks.

**Unverified.** I did not test the Lion's Eye Diamond line. The deck is mostly enchantments, so a hand without enough of them makes the combo weak. Entomb, Vampiric Tutor, Demonic Tutor and Wheel of Fortune are banned or not legal in Premodern, which is why I didn't use black or red enablers.

results.prompt: Build a Modern deck around Thassa's Oracle and Tainted Pact.
results.text:
**Tainted Pact isn't legal in Modern.** The card database lists it as "not legal". Demonic Consultation, the other "exile your whole library" card, is also not legal. I built the closest legal version of the combo instead. It is a brew with no proven list behind it, and I have not goldfished it.

**Plan:** Mill and dredge your own library down to a few cards, then win with Thassa's Oracle or Laboratory Maniac. Thassa's Oracle wins when your devotion to blue is at least the number of cards in your library. Laboratory Maniac wins when you would draw from an empty library.

**Key cards:**
- **Spoils of the Vault:** This is the legal stand-in for Tainted Pact. Name a card that isn't in your library and it exiles the whole library. You lose 1 life per card exiled, so you can only fire it once the library is under about 15 cards. Then you cast Oracle with an empty library.
- **Oracle and Maniac:** There are 4 Oracles and 2 Maniacs, so one of them shows up often enough. I didn't run the draw odds.
- **Mill engine:** Hedron Crab, Stitcher's Supplier, Thought Scour, Otherworldly Gaze and 2 Traumatize (half your library) do the milling. Stinkweed Imp and Golgari Thug are dredgers that mill 5 and 4 in place of a draw. A dredge into an empty library also sets up Maniac.
- **Disruption:** 3 Inquisition of Kozilek and 2 Fatal Push give a little protection while you set up.

**Mana:** The deck has 22 lands: 3 Watery Grave, 3 Undercity Sewers, 2 Dismal Backwater, 3 Polluted Delta, 6 Island, 4 Swamp and 1 Dakmor Salvage. That gives 17 blue sources and 16 black sources. The tool's recommendation is about 20 lands, but Hedron Crab wants land drops. Dismal Backwater gains life, which helps Spoils. The check_deck run on the mana raised no errors or warnings.

**Sideboard:** It has 3 Thoughtseize, 2 Surgical Extraction, 2 Consign to Memory, 2 Mystical Dispute, 2 Spell Snare, 2 Fatal Push, 1 Go for the Throat and 1 Engineered Explosives.
- **Broodscale Combo, Blink and Devoted Druid Combo:** Bring in Thoughtseize and Consign to Memory. Consign counters triggered abilities and colorless spells.
- **Goryo's Vengeance, Living End and Frog:** Bring in Surgical Extraction and Spell Snare.
- **Prowess, Zoo, Affinity and Energy:** Bring in Fatal Push and Go for the Throat, and Engineered Explosives against Affinity. Take out the slow Traumatize and some Inquisitions.
- **Storm and other combo decks:** Bring in Mystical Dispute and Thoughtseize.

**Unverified:** I didn't check how fast the deck assembles or how it does against the current field. It will probably be slower than Broodscale Combo, which is the biggest share of recent results at 14.4%. Spoils of the Vault costs you life equal to your library size, and Watery Grave and Polluted Delta cost life too, so sequence them carefully.

results.prompt: I want a Modern Merfolk deck that can beat the current top decks.
results.text:
I built a mono-blue Merfolk deck and the tool accepted it. It's a tuned version of the 5-0 Modern League Merfolk list. I changed two cards in the main deck and a few in the sideboard.

**Plan:** Play cheap Merfolk, then put the lords on the table: Lord of Atlantis, Master of the Pearl Trident, Vodalian Hexcatcher and Svyelun of Sea and Sky. Your Merfolk get +1/+1 and islandwalk. Harbinger of the Seas turns every nonbasic land into an Island, so opposing nonbasic lands also enable islandwalk. Counterspells and bounce protect the clock.

**Key cards:**
- **Aether Vial and Cavern of Souls:** Vial puts creatures onto the battlefield around counterspells. Cavern, named for Merfolk, makes them uncounterable.
- **Silvergill Adept and Tide Shaper:** These are the cheap starts. Silvergill Adept draws a card, and Tide Shaper turns a land into an Island when kicked.
- **Flare of Denial, Sink into Stupor, Snapback:** Flare of Denial can be cast for free by sacrificing a nontoken blue creature. Sink into Stupor is a bounce spell that doubles as a land. Snapback returns a creature to hand.
- **Tishana's Tidebinder (2 copies):** I added these in place of 2 Snapbacks. It has flash, and it counters a triggered or activated ability. That matters against Broodscale Combo, the biggest deck at 14.4% of recent results, and against Blink at 5.9%.

**Mana:** The deck has 16 real lands: 7 Island, 4 Cavern of Souls, 3 Mutavault and 2 Otawara. Sink into Stupor adds 4 more land-capable cards. The check tool's land warning came back empty. It reports 15 blue sources, against a real-list average of about 15.9 blue sources for Merfolk. The curve tops out at 3 mana.

**Sideboard (15):**
- **Consign to Memory ×4:** It counters triggered abilities and colorless spells. That hits Broodscale Combo, Affinity and Eldrazi Tron. Bring it in against any of these decks.
- **Chalice of the Void ×3:** It's strong against Eldrazi Tron, Devoted Druid Combo, Affinity and Broodscale at 1 or 2 counters. Cut it against decks that don't care about cheap spells, and keep in mind your own deck is full of 1- and 2-drops.
- **Force of Negation ×3:** It counters noncreature spells and can be free on the opponent's turn. Use it against Goryo's Vengeance, Frog, Living End, Storm, Prowess and control decks.
- **Subtlety ×3:** It's a flash flier that puts a creature spell back in the library. Bring it in against Living End and Frog.
- **Ghost Vacuum ×2:** It exiles cards from graveyards. Bring it in against Goryo's Vengeance and Living End.

When you're on the play against a fast deck, trim slower cards like Silvergill Adept for the free counters.

**What I couldn't verify:**
- I didn't test win rates. The only evidence is that the base list went 5-0, and Merfolk had only 14 recent lists.
- I swapped 2 Snapback for Tidebinder and chose the sideboard split from the meta data, not from tournament testing. The unchanged 4-of Chalice, Consign, Force and Subtlety sideboard from the proven list is a safe fallback.

results.prompt: Make a fun mono white control deck for Modern leagues.
results.text:
I built a mono-white control brew for Modern. It has no proven list behind it, so it is untested. It borrows only the mana philosophy and a few staples from the UW Control archetype in the results.

**Plan:** Stay alive with cheap interaction, flexible sweepers and Wall of Omens. Then take over with planeswalkers that make their own army, and Solitude as a free answer when you're behind.

**Key cards:**
- **Wrath of the Skies (3)** is the flexible sweeper. It's {X}{W}{W}, so it works as a cheap answer to small threats or a full wrath. It shows up in about 28% of recent lists.
- **Solitude (4)** can be evoked by exiling a white card, which makes it a free answer to fast decks. It's very common in recent results.
- **Spot removal:** Path to Exile (2), March of Otherworldly Light (3), Stroke of Midnight (2), Generous Gift (1) and Prismatic Ending (2). Prismatic Ending only hits mana value 1 or less in a one-colour deck. I kept it to 2 copies for Broodscale and other 1-drops.
- **Orim's Chant (2) and Reprieve (1)** cover the combo decks (Broodscale, Storm, Goryo's). A kicked Chant also works as a one-turn fog.
- **Win conditions:**
  - Elspeth, Storm Slayer (2) doubles the tokens it makes. That includes its own soldiers, Wandering Emperor's Samurai and Fountainport's Fish.
  - Elspeth, Sun's Champion, The Eternal Wanderer, Archangel Avacyn and Elspeth Conquers Death round out the top end.
  - The Wandering Emperor (2) has flash.
- **Card flow:** Wall of Omens (4) and Spirited Companion (2).

**Mana:** 24 lands, with 22 of them making white. That is 18 Plains, 2 Secluded Steppe (cycling), Eiganjo (a removal spell in land form), Monumental Henge (digs for legendary cards, Sagas and artifacts), Fountainport and Field of Ruin. The tool recommended about 21 lands. I went higher because the curve has eight 5-drops and two 6-drops, and the Walls and cyclers smooth it out. Colourless lands are limited to two because of the WW costs.

**Sideboarding:** The sideboard has 15 cards.
- **Broodscale, Affinity, Eldrazi Tron:** Bring in 2 Cathar Commando, 2 Stony Silence and Loran. Take out the Spirited Companions and Generous Gift.
- **Living End, Goryo's Vengeance, Rakdos Delirium, Frog:** Bring in 2 Rest in Peace and Containment Priest. Take out the slow 5-drops such as Settle the Wreckage and Elspeth Conquers Death. Rest in Peace shuts off Living End and Goryo's, though it also exiles your own graveyard.
- **Storm and Prowess:** Bring in 2 High Noon, Mana Tithe and Sanctifier en-Vec. High Noon limits each player to one spell a turn. Sanctifier en-Vec has protection from black and red.
- **Energy and red decks:** Bring in 2 Celestial Purge and Sanctifier en-Vec.
- **Creature-heavy matchups:** Add Sunfall. Cut a Path or Prismatic Ending.

**Unverified:** I didn't simulate matchups or check win rates. Swords to Plowshares, Council's Judgment and Karakas are not Modern-legal, so they are not in the deck.

**Plan:** Play a one-drop on turn 1, then keep adding cheap creatures and burn. Rally at the Hornburg and Goblin Bushwhacker give the whole team haste for a big attack. Burn finishes the game or clears a blocker. The curve is almost all one-drops: 32 cards cost 1 and 11 cost 2.

**Key cards:**
- **Burning-Tree Emissary, Clockwork Percussionist, Goblin Tomb Raider, Voldaren Epicure, Gingerbrute:** These are the cheap threats, and most of them (all but Epicure) also have haste or can get it.
- **Percussionist, Gingerbrute and the Epicure's Blood token:** These are artifacts, which turn on Tomb Raider's +1/+0 and haste.
- **Rally at the Hornburg:** It makes two 1/1 Humans and gives Humans haste for the turn. Every list in the archetype data plays four.

If you flood less than you stumble, add a Mountain and cut the End the Festivities.

results.prompt: Build a Pioneer deck around Greasefang, Okiba Boss that isn't the usual list.
results.text:
**The deck:** Orzhov "Greasefang Garage". It's a brew, and the submitted list passed check_deck with no errors or warnings.

**Plan.** The usual Greasefang list is a green-splash combo deck that discards Parhelion II and cheats it out. This list uses Greasefang, Okiba Boss as a repeatable removal engine instead. Most of the vehicles have enters-the-battlefield effects, and Greasefang returns one to the battlefield each combat. At the beginning of your next end step the vehicle returns to your hand, so you can recast it for the same effect again.

**Key cards**
- **Skysovereign, Consul Flagship (3 copies):** It deals 3 damage to a creature or planeswalker when it enters and again when it attacks.
- **The Fire Nation Drill (2), Surgehacker Mech (2), Unidentified Hovership (2):** Each removes a creature when it enters. The Drill destroys a creature with power 4 or less, the Mech deals damage equal to twice your vehicle count, and the Hovership exiles a creature with toughness 5 or less.
- **Parhelion II (1):** A single copy as the finisher. I didn't build the deck around it.
- **Smuggler's Copter (3), Professor of Symbology (4), Overlord of the Balemurk (3), Fleeting Spirit (3), Rotting Regisaur (2):** These put vehicles in the graveyard by looting, discarding or milling. The Overlord can also return a Greasefang you've lost.
- **Rotting Regisaur:** Its upkeep discard also feeds the graveyard. The cost is that it empties your hand over time.
- **Interaction:** Fatal Push (4), Bitter Triumph (3) and Thoughtseize (2). Bitter Triumph's discard cost can also put a vehicle in the graveyard.

**Mana.** It has 22 lands, all white and black: 4 Concealed Courtyard, 4 Godless Shrine, 2 Caves of Koilos, 2 Brightclimb Pathway, 2 Bleachbone Verge, 2 Shadowy Backstreet, Takenuma, 3 Plains and 2 Swamp. That gives 19 white sources and 19 black sources. check_deck suggests 24.5 lands, so I'm running light. I'm relying on the cheap curve and the looting, but add a land if you flood less than you stumble.

**Sideboard**
- **Against Mono-Red and Izzet Prowess, and other aggro decks:** Bring in Pest Control (2) and Collective Brutality (2). Take out Thoughtseize and the slow 5-drop Skysovereigns.
- **Against Golgari Midrange and Jund Sacrifice:** Bring in Duress (2) and Vanishing Verse (2).
- **Against Greasefang mirrors, Lessons, Phoenix and Cauldron:** Bring in Soul-Guide Lantern (3) and Unlicensed Hearse (2), and cut the Overlords.
- **Mysterious Limousine and Detention Chariot** are hard-cast answers to a single threat. I left them out of the main deck on purpose. If Greasefang returns either to your hand at end of turn, the exiled creature comes back.

**Unverified.** I haven't tested the draw odds or how the deck plays in practice. I picked the 3-drop and 4-drop vehicle counts by feel.

results.prompt: Make a Vintage artifact aggro deck.

**Plan:** Cast cheap artifact creatures on turn one or two with Moxen, Lotus, Crypt, Sol Ring, Workshop and Ancient Tomb. Then grow them and attack before the Lurrus, Paradoxical Outcome and Oath decks, which make up much of the metagame, get going.

**Key cards**
- **Creatures:**
  - Patchwork Automaton ×4 gets a +1/+1 counter for each artifact spell you cast.
  - Glaring Fleshraker ×4 makes Spawn tokens when you cast a colorless spell and pings the opponent whenever another colorless creature enters.
  - Scrawling Crawler ×3, Stonecoil Serpent ×2, Walking Ballista, Hangarback Walker ×2, Steel Overseer ×2 and Chief of the Foundry ×2 fill out the curve.
  - Foundry Inspector, Lodestone Golem, Memnite and Ornithopter are the other creatures. Memnite and Ornithopter are free Fleshraker triggers and Urza's Saga targets.
  - Wurmcoil Engine and Myr Battlesphere are the top end, and Workshop mana makes them castable early.

results.prompt: Build me a Premodern Dream Halls deck that doesn't win with storm.
results.text:
I built a Premodern Dream Halls deck that wins with Seismic Assault and burn instead of Brain Freeze or any other storm finisher. It's a brew, so there's no tournament list behind it. I didn't playtest it, and I didn't run draw-odds checks on the chain.

**Plan:** Get Dream Halls onto the battlefield with a 5-mana cast or a 3-mana Show and Tell, helped by Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors and Lotus Petal. Then pitch blue cards to cast the draw spells for free. Dream Halls itself has mana value 5, so Rush of Knowledge draws at least 5 cards with it out. Opportunity and Meditate draw 4. Frantic Search and the cantrips fill the gaps.

**Why the win condition works:** Laboratory Maniac and Thassa's Oracle aren't legal in Premodern, so I couldn't build a decking win. Once the chain has filled your hand with lands, Seismic Assault turns each discarded land into 2 damage. The deck runs 2 copies, and Dream Halls lets you cast it by pitching any red card. Show and Tell can also put it onto the battlefield for 3 mana. The finishing burn is two Prophetic Bolt (4 damage each) and two Fire // Ice (2 damage). Palinchron is a one-of backup that makes Rush draw 7 and untaps your lands. Prophetic Bolt and Fire // Ice share both colors with blue and red spells. That means they can be discarded to cast either kind for free.

**Why these cards:**
- **Intuition and Cunning Wish** find Dream Halls or the finishers. Cunning Wish can also fetch sideboard instants such as Fireblast, Chain of Vapor and Stifle.
- **Arcane Denial** is the only protection main deck. I didn't add white for Orim's Chant, which many existing lists use.

**Mana:** 19 lands plus 3 Lotus Petal. The lands are 4 Ancient Tomb, 1 City of Traitors, 2 Svyelunite Temple, 2 Saprazzan Skerry, 3 Shivan Reef and 7 Island. That gives 17 blue sources and 6 red, and the red mostly exists so the red cards can be pitched. check_deck warned that 6 red sources is low for casting Seismic Assault on curve. I accepted that because the deck casts it for free, and the blue count is in line with real Dream Halls lists.

**Sideboard (15):** Fireblast, 2 Chain of Vapor, 2 Blue Elemental Blast, 1 Hydroblast, 2 Defense Grid, 2 Annul, 1 Stifle, 1 Rushing River, 1 Teferi's Response, 1 Red Elemental Blast, 1 Tormod's Crypt.
- **Sligh and Goblins:** bring in the Blue Elemental Blasts, Hydroblast and Chain of Vapor. Cut Seismic Assault and slow cards like Meditate.
- **Stiflenought and UB Psychatog:** these decks counter a lot. Bring in Stifle, the Red Elemental Blast, Teferi's Response and Defense Grid. Defense Grid makes spells cost 3 more except on their controller's turn, so cast your spells on your own turn.
- **Enchantress:** bring in Annul, Chain of Vapor and Rushing River, because Enchantress's permanents are what you need to answer. Keep Show and Tell, but note it lets the opponent put a permanent in as well.
- **Replenish and Hermit Druid:** bring in Tormod's Crypt and Stifle for their graveyard and triggered-ability plans.
- **Terrageddon:** bring in the Blue Elemental Blasts, since Terrageddon lists run red cards.

Dream Halls works for your opponent too. Don't leave it out against decks that can pitch cards freely.

warnings: 6 R sources; Seismic Assault wants about 23 to cast on curve.

results.prompt: Build a deck that best utilizes Peter Parker's Camera.
results.text:
I built a Modern UW artifact deck that plays three Peter Parker's Camera. It is a tuned version of the Emry list that went 5-0 in a Modern League on 2026-10-12. Camera is legal in Modern and costs {1}. Its text is "{2}, {T}, remove a film counter: copy target activated or triggered ability you control." It enters with three film counters.

**Plan:** Cheap artifacts power Mox Opal's metalcraft and make Emry and Urza cost almost nothing. Camera is both an artifact and a way to double the deck's best abilities. It can double Urza's Construct trigger, Urza's Saga's Construct ability, Tamiyo's Clue-on-attack trigger, Sewer-veillance Cam's tap/untap trigger, and Skateboard's tap trigger. It also copies a Portable Hole exile.

**Why these cards:**
- **Camera recursion:** Camera is mana value 1, so Urza's Saga chapter III can fetch it. Oswald Fiddlebender can sacrifice a 1-mana artifact to find a 2-mana artifact. Emry can recast Camera from the graveyard, and it comes back with three fresh film counters. Camera is no longer limited to three uses.
- **Loki, God of Mischief:** I dropped Loki from the 5-0 list's main deck. The ability that triggers Loki's draw is the one Camera copies, but it only draws once per turn, so it adds little.
- **Cuts:** To make room I cut Sword of the Meek, Thopter Foundry and Disruptor Flute. Those are low-impact in a 3-Camera build.
- **Interaction:** Portable Hole, Metallic Rebuke and Pithing Needle stay for interaction. The Needle is aimed at Broodscale Combo, the biggest deck in the meta at 14.4%.

**Mana:** 18 lands, which matches the Emry average of 17.94. The deck has 23 blue sources and 17 white sources, and the average mana value is 1.33. The check_deck tool flagged no errors or warnings. It did note 18 lands against a recommended 19.7, but this is a very low curve with 11 zero-cost artifacts.

**Sideboard:** I kept the 5-0 list's 15 cards.
- **Broodscale, Eldrazi Tron, Affinity and Energy:** Bring in Consign to Memory (it counters triggered abilities and colorless spells) and Damping Sphere. Add Vexing Bauble and the second Force of Negation, and board out Camera and the slower Emry value cards.
- **Prowess and Blink:** Bring in March of Otherworldly Light and Test of Talents. March exiles artifacts, creatures and enchantments, and Test of Talents counters instants and sorceries.
- **Control and creature-light matchups:** Bring in the two Teferi, Time Raveler and The Theorist, Jace Beleren. Teferi's −3 is a good Camera target because the copy doubles the bounce and the card draw.

**Label:** Tuned, not a new brew. Camera is only a one-of or two-of in tournament lists so far (two Modern lists in the last 90 days), so there is no proven list built around it. I did not run a matchup simulation, so I can't give win rates. Camera costs 2 per use and has only three counters, so the gain is value, not a combo.

results.prompt: Build a Commander deck with Atraxa, Praetors' Voice that's all about proliferate.
results.text:
The deck is submitted and `check_deck` passed with no errors or warnings. It's a brew: the tools returned no tournament data for Commander, so nothing here is copied from a proven list.

**Plan:** Ramp into Atraxa, Praetors' Voice on turn 3 or 4. Her end-step proliferate then grows planeswalker loyalty, +1/+1 counters and poison every turn. The deck can win three ways:
- Planeswalker ultimates.
- Counter-doubling effects on creatures and Walking Ballista.
- Poison from toxic and infect-style creatures, boosted by Winding Constrictor and Vorinclex.

**Key cards:**
- **Extra proliferate sources (about 20):**
  - Evolution Sage, Thrummingbird, Ezuri, Tromell, Bloated Contaminator, Metastatic Evangel, Flux Channeler, Tainted Observer and Merfolk Skydiver proliferate on their own triggers.
  - Inexorable Tide, Karn's Bastion, Contagion Clasp, Contagion Engine, Glistening Sphere and the proliferate spells add more.
  - Tekuthal makes every proliferate happen twice.
  - Ezuri draws a card each time you proliferate.
- **Counter multipliers:** Doubling Season, Vorinclex, Hardened Scales, Winding Constrictor, Corpsejack Menace, Innkeeper's Talent, Ozolith, Conclave Mentor and Deepglow Skate. Vorinclex also doubles the counters your proliferate adds.
- **Counter targets:** Nine planeswalkers, plus Walking Ballista and Hangarback Walker. The planeswalkers are Oko, Grist, Nissa Who Shakes the World, Elspeth Sun's Champion, Teferi Hero of Dominaria, both Vraskas (Relic Seeker and Golgari Queen), Ajani Sleeper Agent and Garruk Relentless. Vraska, Betrayal's Sting is a tenth that proliferates itself.
- **Interaction:** Swords, Path, Assassin's Trophy, Anguished Unmaking, Toxic Deluge, Cyclonic Rift, Beast Within and Heroic Intervention, plus Drown in Ichor and Atomize, which proliferate as they remove. I left out Mana Crypt because the card pool lists it as banned.

**Mana:** The deck has 35 lands and 12 ramp pieces, with an average mana value of 2.88. Source counts are about 17.5 white, 18.5 blue, 17.5 black and 20 green. I replaced Counterspell, Elspeth Knight-Errant and Liliana, Death's Majesty with cards that need less of one color. That cleared the double-colored-cost warnings from `check_deck`. The fixing is:
- 6 shocklands.
- 3 triomes and 2 tri-lands.
- 6 checklands.
- 6 fetchlands, which also trigger Evolution Sage's landfall.
- Command Tower, Starting Town and Fabled Passage.
- 8 basics (3 Forest, 2 Island, 2 Swamp, 1 Plains) for the land-fetch spells.

**Sideboard:** Commander has no sideboard, so there are no 15 cards. Adjust to your table by swapping flex slots:
- **Against creature decks:** Toxic Deluge and Elspeth Sun's Champion handle go-wide boards. Add more removal in place of Venser or Scheming Aspirant.
- **Against combo or control:** Cyclonic Rift, Rhystic Study and Heroic Intervention protect your engine. Consider adding Mana Drain or Swan Song if blue is your lean.
- **Against artifact or enchantment decks:** Beast Within and Assassin's Trophy are your answers. Boseiju or Reclamation Sage could replace weaker proliferate pieces.

**Not verified:**
- I haven't playtested this.
- Win speed depends on your pod. This is a value and planeswalker deck, not a fast combo deck.
- I didn't run draw odds, because nothing in the deck is a combo that has to be assembled.

results.prompt: Build an aggressive Duel Commander deck with a red commander.
results.text:
**Laelia, the Blade Reforged** leads a mono-red haste-and-burn deck. It's a brew, and the 99 cards are legal in Duel Commander (check_deck returned no errors). The tool's only warning said 35 lands is low, and I kept 35 anyway. That count is close to the 36.3 the Zurgo Bellstriker mono-red lists average.

**Plan:** Cheap hasty creatures put the opponent under pressure by turn 3. Burn then clears blockers or goes to the face. Laelia is a 3-mana haste creature that grows each time it attacks. It also exiles the top card of your library each attack, and you can play that card that turn. If the opponent kills her, the commander tax stays small.

**Key cards**
- **Early pressure:** Goblin Guide, Monastery Swiftspear, Slickshot Show-Off, Emberheart Challenger and Goblin Rabblemaster.
- **Burn:** Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning, Fireblast, Skewer the Critics and Skullcrack finish games. Flame Slash, Fanged Flames, Mizzium Mortars and Pyrokinesis clear blockers. Burn is about a quarter of the deck.
- **Equipment:** Umezawa's Jitte, Sword of Fire and Ice, Embercleave and Cori-Steel Cutter make any small creature a threat.
- **Top end:** Hellrider and Glorybringer.
- **Removal and utility:** Fury, Chandra, Torch of Defiance, Fable of the Mirror-Breaker and Delayed Blast Fireball.
- **Banned cards:** Ragavan, Sol Ring, Mana Crypt, Chrome Mox and Ancient Tomb all showed as banned, so none are in the deck.

**Mana:** The deck has 33 real lands plus 4 spell-lands that can be played as lands: Spikefield Hazard, Kazuul's Fury, Shatterskull Smashing and Sundering Eruption. The lands are 24 Mountain, 4 red fetches (Arid Mesa, Scalding Tarn, Bloodstained Mire, Wooded Foothills), Prismatic Vista, Arena of Glory, Barbarian Ring, Shinka and Sokenzan. Enough basic Mountains stay in the deck to power Fireblast and Mine Collapse, and the fetches thin the deck. The average mana value is 2.35. I based the land count and mana on the Zurgo Bellstriker 5-0 list.

**Sideboard:** Duel Commander has no sideboard, so I didn't build one. The answers have to be in the main deck. The meta data shows these decks:
- **Cloud, Midgar Mercenary:** the most common deck, at 11% of results. It plays Umezawa's Jitte and Sword of Fire and Ice. Abrade, Chaos Warp and Pyrokinesis answer its equipment and creatures. Use Jitte and Sword of Fire and Ice yourself, since Sword gives protection from red and blue.
- **Token and creature decks (Slimefoot and Squee, Aragorn):** Forked Bolt, Chainwhirler, Delayed Blast Fireball, Fury and Mizzium Mortars (overloaded) handle wide boards.
- **Slower value decks (Brigid, Jace, Tasigur):** Goblin Guide, Hellrider, Fireblast and Skullcrack are meant to kill them before their card advantage matters.

**Unverified:** The meta tool showed no red deck built around Laelia. The card choices come from how the Zurgo Bellstriker list is built and from card text, not from results for this exact deck. I did not simulate it. I also dropped Eidolon of the Great Revel, which that list plays. This deck casts many cheap spells, so Eidolon would hurt its owner as well.

results.prompt: Something weird but competitive for Premodern.
results.text:
I submitted a stock Aluren list in Premodern. It's the most recent 5-0 Premodern League list, copied unchanged. Aluren was about 1.3% of the field in the last 30 days, so it's a weird choice but not an untested one.

**Plan:** Resolve Aluren, which says any player may cast creature spells with mana value 3 or less for free and at instant speed. After that, chain cheap creatures that return each other to hand:
- **Loop pieces:** Cavern Harpy, Man-o'-War and Raven Familiar, plus Whirlpool Rider and Wall of Blossoms.
- **Harpy:** Cavern Harpy returns a blue or black creature when it enters, and you can pay 1 life to bounce it back to your hand.
- **Man-o'-War and Raven Familiar:** Each triggers when it enters, so replaying them for free gives you repeated bounce and card selection.
- **Finishers:** Ghitu Slinger deals 2 damage when it enters. Squee, Goblin Nabob and Spike Feeder help the loop keep going. Academy Rector can fetch Aluren if the first one is destroyed.

**Why these cards:**
- **Survival of the Fittest** and Cabal Therapy are the two flexible cards. Survival turns any creature into the exact piece you need. Therapy strips counterspells or removal before you go off.
- **Birds of Paradise** and Wall of Roots give you a turn-two Aluren.
- The Wall of Blossoms, Raven Familiar and Whirlpool Rider all dig toward the engine.

**Mana:** It runs 23 lands plus three mana creatures. The lands are Yavimaya Coast, Llanowar Wastes, City of Brass, Reflecting Pool, Gemstone Mine, 4 Havenwood Battleground and 5 Forest. `check_deck` reports about 24 green sources, 12 blue and 11 black, with no errors or warnings against real Aluren lists.

**Sideboarding:**
- **Enchantress (12.5%) and Terrageddon (11.2%):** Bring in Naturalize, Xantid Swarm and Compost. Xantid Swarm stops them casting spells on your turn. Naturalize clears their enchantments and artifacts.
- **Stiflenought (10.4%) and UB Psychatog (4.8%):** Bring in Tsabo's Web, which also draws a card. Add Tormod's Crypt against Psychatog and Replenish.
- **Replenish (4.8%) and Hermit Druid (5.5%):** Bring in Tormod's Crypt and the extra Cabal Therapy.
- **Sligh (9.9%):** Take out Cabal Therapy and a few slow pieces, and add Tsabo's Web. The deck has limited answers to burn. Aluren's free creatures blocking and chump-blocking are the main defense.

**Label:** Stock. I didn't change any card. The only thing I checked in this session was the list's legality.

**Not verified:** I didn't playtest the matchups, so the sideboard plans are my own reasoning. They aren't backed by matchup win rates.
